Resonator instruments are wired with inverted polarity, opposite frequency encoding, or different reference standards since Day 1 setup; anti-correlation is a signature of systematic inversion, not noise or transient.

Day 30 transient environmental or mechanical shock (seismic, building vibration, thermal, power transient) triggered acute excursions in both resonator instruments simultaneously; baseline and post-shock behavior are both valid, but the shock explains the Day 30 variance spike without changing the underlying inversion hypothesis.

Baseline period (days 1–10) was incompletely settled; instruments are undergoing multi-phase equilibration with a secondary transition around Day 20–30; the Day 30 variance spike marks onset of stable post-equilibration state, and inversion (if present) is a separate configuration issue.

Unlogged operational or environmental confound (temperature, humidity, time-of-day, operator, warm-up duration, vibration) correlated with trial sequence, settlement activity, or Day 30 event; confound biases all cross-correlations and produced Day 30 anomalies independently of hardware state.

Single resonator hardware fault (resonator_lab only: loss of lock, frequency drift, sensor bridge imbalance, or component aging since Day 1) accounts for the anti-correlation signature by causing progressive de-calibration of one arm of the resonator pair.

Residual: unrecorded metadata, instrument configuration error at Day 1 setup not yet identified, or settlement-wide environmental event not visible in current notebooks (e.g., power supply transient affecting frequency reference, ground loop coupling between instruments, or site-wide vibration from unknown source).
